name: Fernando de Noronha
tagline: A protected volcanic archipelago far out in the Atlantic, with some of Brazil's best beaches, spinner dolphins, sea turtles and diving, and strictly limited visitor numbers.
highlight: The Baía do Sancho at sunrise, reached down a cliff-side ladder to an empty crescent of sand.
shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed island 350 km off the north-east coast, with turquoise bays, marine life, snorkelling, diving and a low-key, high-price resort atmosphere.
metaDescription: A Fernando de Noronha travel guide: Baía do Sancho, Baía dos Porcos, Morro Dois Irmãos, spinner dolphins, sea turtles, diving, fees and limits, best time, how to get there and a four-day plan.
knownFor: Beaches, diving, dolphins, turtles, protected environment
budget: US$200–400 per day, mid-range; the island is expensive

image.file: File:Fernando De Noronha Strand Baia Do Sancho (125363049).jpeg
image.alt: The turquoise water and white sand of Baía do Sancho beach on Fernando de Noronha

intro: Fernando de Noronha is an archipelago of 21 islands and islets about 350 km off the coast of north-east Brazil, the tips of an underwater volcanic chain. Only the main island is inhabited, with about 3,000 residents, and about 70% of it is a national marine park. UNESCO inscribed the islands in 2001 as part of the Brazilian Atlantic Islands.

The archipelago's beaches, bays and cliffs are widely considered the best in Brazil, and Baía do Sancho has been ranked among the best beaches in the world. The waters are warm and clear, with visibility often more than 30 metres, and full of marine life, including green turtles, spinner dolphins, rays and sharks. Diving and snorkelling are outstanding.

Because of its protected status, visits are tightly controlled. There are daily visitor limits, a mandatory environmental preservation fee that rises with length of stay, and separate park entry tickets. The island is expensive, but it is also unspoilt, quiet and beautiful, with pousadas, small restaurants and buggies, and a relaxed pace. The dry season from August to January is best.

whyVisit.intro: Noronha is one of the best places in Brazil for beaches and marine wildlife, in a carefully protected environment.

points.title: Superb beaches
points.text: Baía do Sancho, Baía dos Porcos and Praia do Leão, among the best in Brazil.

points.title: Diving and snorkelling
points.text: Clear water, wrecks and abundant marine life.

points.title: Dolphins and turtles
points.text: Spinner dolphins gather in the Baía dos Golfinhos, and turtles nest on beaches.

points.title: A protected paradise
points.text: Visitor limits and strict rules keep it unspoilt.

points.title: Tranquillity
points.text: A slow pace, sunsets and stars.

attractionsIntro: The beaches and viewpoints are close together, and easily reached by buggy or on foot.

attractions.name: Baía do Sancho
attractions.text: A hidden bay with white sand and turquoise water below cliffs, reached by a steep path and a ladder in the rock. Widely ranked among the world's best beaches.
attractions.tip: Go early, and do not touch the reef.

attractions.name: Baía dos Porcos and Praia do Leão
attractions.text: A bay with natural tidal pools and calm snorkelling, and a beach where turtles nest at night in season.

attractions.name: Morro Dois Irmãos

image.file: File:Morro Dois Irmãos - Fernando de Noronha.jpg
image.alt: The twin rock peaks of Morro Dois Irmãos rising from the sea at Fernando de Noronha

attractions.text: The island's iconic twin peaks, which rise from the water at Sancho and Porcos bays.
attractions.tip: Admire them from the beach and the boat.

attractions.name: Baía dos Golfinhos
attractions.text: A bay where spinner dolphins gather in the morning, seen from a lookout. Boat approaches are prohibited to protect them.

attractions.name: Sea turtles

image.file: File:Parque Nacional Marinho de Fernando de Noronha - João Paulo Marques DAndretta 12.jpg
image.alt: A green sea turtle swimming over the reef at Fernando de Noronha

attractions.text: Green turtles are often seen snorkelling, and the Tamar Project protects nesting beaches.

attractions.name: Forte dos Remédios and Vila dos Remédios
attractions.text: A historic fort and the village, the island's small centre with a church, restaurants and sunset views.

thingsToDoIntro: Water activities dominate, with a few land experiences.

thingsToDo.title: Snorkel with turtles
thingsToDo.text: Baía do Sancho and Baía dos Porcos have clear water and marine life.

thingsToDo.title: Dive the reefs and wrecks
thingsToDo.text: Excellent diving for beginners and experts.

thingsToDo.title: Watch dolphins from the lookout
thingsToDo.text: Spinner dolphins gather in the morning.

thingsToDo.title: Take a boat trip
thingsToDo.text: Sail around the island, with stops for snorkelling.

thingsToDo.title: Go on an island buggy tour
thingsToDo.text: Explore beaches and viewpoints by rented buggy.

thingsToDo.title: Watch the sunset at Forte dos Remédios
thingsToDo.text: A traditional way to end the day.

foodIntro: Food on the island is seafood, and prices are high because of transport costs.

foods.name: Fresh fish
foods.text: Tuna, wahoo and other pelagic fish, grilled or in stews.

foods.name: Tapioca and coconut
foods.text: Cassava pancakes, and fresh coconut water.

foods.name: Caipirinha
foods.text: The national cocktail, with local flavours.

accommodation.intro: Accommodation is mainly small pousadas, and prices are high. Book well ahead.

gettingThere.intro: The island is reached only by air, from Recife or Natal.

options.text: About 1 hour 20 minutes, with daily flights.
options.detail: Book early, as seats are limited.

options.text: Some cruises stop at the island, but landing is limited.

gettingAround.intro: The island is small, and buggies are the main way to move.

options.text: Serve the main roads and beaches.

bestTime.headline: August–January
bestTime.summary: Noronha is warm year-round, with a dry season from August to January and a rainy season from February to July.

seasons.text: Clear skies, calm seas and the best visibility.
Hot and dry, with good conditions.
Warm and showery, with rougher seas and low prices.
Showers, with big surf on the north.

bestTime.avoid: The wettest months, from March to June.

itinerary.title: Four days on Fernando de Noronha

tipsIntro: The island has strict rules and high prices.
tips: Book flights and accommodation many months ahead.
Pay the environmental fee and buy park tickets in advance.
Use reef-safe sunscreen and do not touch marine life.
Do not use plastic straws or bring single-use items.
Bring cash, since ATMs are limited.
Stay a minimum of four days to make the trip worthwhile.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Fernando de Noronha?
faq.a: Four to five days is ideal.
Yes. Accommodation, food and fees are high, partly because of the island's isolation and protected status.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?

faq.a: No. Contact with spinner dolphins is prohibited. You can watch them from the lookout.
By flight from Recife or Natal.

faq.q: Do I need to pay fees?
faq.a: Yes, an environmental preservation fee and a national park entry ticket. Check current prices.
